Definition: from G2209; to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment:--be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss.
BiblicalUsage: To suffer loss is what this verb describes, and Jesus puts it in the starkest terms: what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his own soul? Mark and Luke carry the same question, and Paul picks the verb up again for the builder whose work burns — saved, ‘yet so as by fire,’ having suffered loss. The loss is real in every case, but the scale of it depends entirely on what is lost.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jesus' question has no comfortable answer, and that is the point. A soul is not one possession among many; it is the person, and no amount of world gained can cover losing it. I believe the warning is also a mercy — it tells me the loss plainly while there is still time to choose otherwise.
